title: Priority-aware traffic quarantine and state-drain experimentation for active-passive DR
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Objective: Validate an active->passive failover sequence that isolates noisy tenants via priority-aware traffic quarantine, gracefully drains in-flight state (KV/prefix-caches), and exercises circuit-breaker cascades and load-shedding rules without violating high-priority SLOs. This ticket captures the experiment plan, automated validation harness, measurable success criteria, and follow-up remediation tasks. Motivation: previous drills recovered services but sometimes caused high-request retries and tokenstore races during bulk promotions. We want a repeatable sequence that minimizes cross-tenant impact, prevents cascading circuit-breaker trips, and proves backup/restore integrity for stateful components.
acceptance_criteria: Can execute a controlled failover that quarantines <= 10% of low-priority traffic while preserving P99 latency for high-priority customers within the SLO target (P99 <= 350ms)
KV cache resync post-failover completes within 5 minutes for 95% of keys with no correctness mismatches
No more than 2 cascading circuit-breaker escalations across regional proxies during the drill
Automated restore verification confirms >= 99.99% backup integrity for tokenstore snapshots used during the drill
Runbook updated with observed timings, toggles, and rollback commands; post-drill incident doc created
playbook_steps: Pre-drill: Notify on-call, affected customers, and GCR; capture baseline metrics (latency, error rate, headroom) for last 24h
Step 1 (Quarantine): Apply priority-aware traffic-policy to route low-priority tenants to quarantine pool (rate-limited) and mark high-priority routes as protected
Step 2 (State drain): Trigger graceful drain of active region state handlers; stream KV prefix snapshots to standby with checksum and version markers
Step 3 (Circuit breakers): Temporarily lower circuit-breaker thresholds for quarantine pool to observe fall-through logic; ensure global throttling gates are active
Step 4 (Capacity shift): Simulate regional capacity loss (traffic-siphon) and redirect protected traffic to passive region with pinned model variants
Step 5 (Restore validation): Perform restore from latest tokenstore and KV snapshots into a sandboxed cluster and run the restore-verifier suite (consistency, replay, auth checks)
Step 6 (Observation): Monitor dashboards for 30 minutes post-shift; watch SLOs, retry rates, error budget burn, and cold-start latencies
Step 7 (Rollback): If high-priority P99 breaches or >2 unknown errors occur, execute immediate rollback sequence (see rollback_plan) and escalate to SRE lead
rollback_plan: Immediate: Re-enable traffic routing to original active region and disable quarantine policy. If KV divergence detected, run automated prefix-reconciler in read-only to surface mismatches, then restore last known-good snapshot and replay idempotent operations from the replication log. Notify PM and Customer Success for high-priority customers and schedule follow-up data integrity audit.
